title: Stillness
& Science
destination.copy: Medical cures in the Alps, Ayurveda above the Ganges, longevity clinics on the Spanish Mediterranean, a desert retreat on Qatar’s northern tip — eight houses where a week gives back more than it takes.

page.tagline: Eight retreats where medicine, tradition and rest share one address — from an Alpine cure to Ayurveda above the Ganges, arranged around the body you arrive with.
page.priceLine: Medical & holistic retreats · rates on request

title: Measured, then
mended
paragraphs: Half of this route is clinical. Lanserhof has united naturopathy and cutting-edge medicine above Innsbruck since 1984; Chenot Palace Weggis runs a 5,000 sqm medical spa on the shores of Lake Lucerne; SHA and ZEM bring advanced diagnostics to the Spanish Mediterranean. Each stay opens with a consultation and closes with a plan you take home.

These are not spas with a doctor on call. Programmes run to minimum stays — seven nights at Chenot, and for most of Lanserhof’s and Ananda’s cures — because the diagnostics, the diet and the rest need time to show in the numbers.

title: Where the
healing began
paragraphs: The other half draws on systems older than the clinic. Ananda sits on a hill above Rishikesh, in the birthplace of Ayurveda, Yoga and meditation; tulåh grows out of Kerala, a global centre of Ayurveda today; Zulal is rooted in Traditional Arabic and Islamic Medicine at Qatar’s northernmost tip; Chiva-Som, Asia’s first wellness resort, has practised its six modalities by the sea at Hua Hin since 1995.

None of them is a museum. Each pairs its tradition with a medical team — Western and Ayurvedic physicians at Ananda, a multidisciplinary clinical council at tulåh, doctors, nurses and nutritionists at Zulal — so the oldest ideas arrive with current measurements.

title: The right retreat,
not the nearest
paragraphs: Choosing between them is the work. A fasting cure at Lanserhof, an 850-kilocalorie week at Chenot, a fourteen-night Panchakarma at Ananda and a four-night clinical check at tulåh answer different questions, and the honest first conversation is about which question you are asking.
We arrange the retreat directly, hold the dates while the pre-arrival consultations are done, and route the flights and transfers around the programme rather than the other way round.

quote.text: Rest is not the absence of a plan. On this route, it is the plan.

essentials.title: Choosing a retreat
essentials.copy: Two families on one route. The medical houses — Lanserhof, Chenot, SHA, ZEM — begin with diagnostics and run on protocols; the traditional houses — Ananda, tulåh, Zulal, Chiva-Som — begin with Ayurveda, Thai or Arabic medicine and build the clinic around it. Tell us what you want to change and we will tell you which door.

essentials.title: How long to stay
essentials.copy: Shorter than a week rarely works. Chenot asks for seven nights; most of Ananda’s programmes need seven and Panchakarma fourteen; Lanserhof’s Classic Detox runs seven to twenty-one; tulåh’s journeys run seven, fourteen or twenty-one, with a four-night clinical check as the exception. Chiva-Som, Zulal, SHA and ZEM will take you from three or four.

essentials.title: Before you go
essentials.copy: Every house begins with a consultation, and several begin before you land. tulåh prepares the journey ahead of arrival; Chenot takes you in at three and sends you off at noon; Ananda welcomes guests of fourteen and over; Chiva-Som Hua Hin and Zulal Serenity are for adults.

essentials.title: Getting there
essentials.copy: Lanserhof Lans sits above Innsbruck; Chenot is fifty minutes from Zürich; ZEM is forty-five minutes from Alicante’s airport; Zulal is ninety minutes north of Doha’s; Ananda is a forty-five-minute flight from Delhi and a forty-minute drive; tulåh is twenty-five minutes from Calicut or forty-five by helicopter from Cochin; Chiva-Som is three and a half hours by road from Bangkok. We route every leg.
